In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of a vitamin D-dependent calcium binding protein from the intestine of the chick.
the purification and characterization of the vitamin D-dependent intestinal calcium-binding protein.
the purification of a calcium-binding protein from chicken intestinal mucosa, kidney and cerebrocerebellum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calcium-binding protein is a vitamin D-dependent protein with a molecular weight of 28000 and an isoelectric point around 4.0, which is present in the intestine and kidney of chicks.
the protein purified by this method is indeed chick intestinal calcium-binding protein, which is vitamin D-dependent and heat stable, and that it is not an artifact of the purification procedure.

the protein isolated by the present purification procedure is identical to the vitamin D-dependent calcium binding protein of chick intestinal, kidney and cerebro-cerebellar origin, which has been previously purified and characterized by other investigators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the calcium-binding protein is purified from chick intestine by a simple and reproducible method.

a simple purification procedure, using chromatofocusing, has been established which is applicable to the isolation of calcium-binding proteins from chick intestine, renal cortex and cerebellum and that the proteins thus obtained are identical with the vitamin D-dependent calcium transport proteins.
chromatofocusing is an excellent method for the purification of calcium-binding protein, and that it can be applied to a wide variety of tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the new procedure allows the purification of calcium-binding proteins from chick intestine and kidney with a yield of 10-20% of the total protein, and from chick cerebellum with a yield of more than 30%.
the purification of chick calcium-binding protein is a simple and rapid process.
the calcium-binding protein is a calcium-binding protein, and that the calcium-binding proteins are calcium-binding proteins.
